question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1\text{ or }y<1 \\ \frac{4({x}^{2}-1)(y-1)}{9y}, & 1\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le 4 \\ {F}_{X}(x), & 1\le x\le 2,\,y>4 \\ {F}_{Y}(y), & x>2,\,1\le y\le 4 \\ 1, & x>2,\,y>4.\end{aligned}
$$

where ${F}_{X}$ and ${F}_{Y}$ are the marginal CDFs of $X$ and $Y,$ respectively. Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $1\le x\le 2$ and $1\le y\le 4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14284682/assets/1ad71a3510a24eed2fdeb387c5f615cc6fb569a58bac2d256fad3d3cb68490d4.svg)

Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1, \; y \geq 0.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y) = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x \partial y} F(x,y).
$$

For $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $y \geq 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}(1-{e}^{-y}))) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\frac{∂}{∂y}(1-{e}^{-y})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{-y}) \\  & ={e}^{-y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}) \\  & ={e}^{-y}\cdot 2x \\  & =2x{e}^{-y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Otherwise, $f(x,y) = 0.$

Therefore, we have
